svg.title: Coordinate Family, Title, Debt, and Probate Evidence
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-ownership-verification-coordination; chapter number: 11; title: Coordinate Family, Title, Debt, and Probate Evidence; subtitle: Inherited ownership and an insurable closing are different findings.; caption: NOLA City Archives emphasizes the family tree; Eric Richardson searches owner-indexed liens; Jamel Gibbs distinguishes preliminary title work; Al Nicoletti checks probate and underwriting; housing and Farm Aid presenters address debt.; assumptions note: NOLA City Archives, Eric Richardson, Jamel Gibbs, Al Nicoletti, Farm Aid, and National Housing Resource Center describe complementary responsibilities, not a shared organization. Headcount is unspecified, and the checks below are qualitative completion criteria rather than numerical performance targets.; note: Al Nicoletti warns that a proposed curative order may still fail underwriting. Farm Aid presenters distinguish taxes from foreclosure fees, and National Housing Resource Center presenters distinguish reverse mortgages from ordinary stay-and-pay situations.; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Inherited-property case coordination; headcount: Not specified; focus: Bring the acquisition deed, complete family tree, debts, property conditions, and proposed cure into the same case assessment.; spokes: role: Family-history research; type: Kinship evidence; kpi: Family tree includes deceased siblings and their children, following NOLA City Archives and Nicoletti's warning about undisclosed relatives.; role: Recorded-title research; type: Deed and lien evidence; kpi: Acquisition deed and owner-name searches are examined; Richardson's lien search and Gibbs's preliminary screening remain distinct from a full purchase search.; role: Probate counsel and title underwriting; type: Authority and insurability; kpi: Nicoletti's proposed cure and complaint are put in writing and checked for underwriting acceptance before treating a probate order as closing-ready.; role: Debt and property-condition assessment; type: Financial and environmental exposure; kpi: Tax recipient, payment status, foreclosure fees, mortgage type, and environmental conditions are examined before authorizing probate expenditure.
